skill.name: post-impl-docs
skill.description: Updates repository documentation after implementation by reviewing code changes and aligning README, CHANGELOG, docs, and docstrings.
skill.summary: Keep documentation synchronized with completed code changes.
skill.author: Consiliency

security_audit.summary: All 79 static findings were reviewed and judged to be false positives. The flagged items are Markdown code fences, inline-code examples, documentation URLs, a placeholder API key example, and exception text. No prompt injection, data exfiltration intent, or unauthorized execution behavior was found.

static_findings.snippet: The format is based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/),
- `option` - Optional flag to enable X behavior (default: False)
> **Deprecated**: `old_function()` will be removed in v3.0. Use `new_function()` instead.
Use the `process()` function to process data.
| New feature | Add to Features section | `feat:` entry | If documented |
| Bug fix | No change | `fix:` entry | If affects behavior |
| Breaking change | Update usage examples | `BREAKING:` entry | Update all refs |
| API addition | Add to API section | `feat:` entry | Add API docs |
| Deprecation | Add deprecation note | `deprecate:` entry | Update examples |
| Tests only | No change | `test:` entry | No |

content.value_statement: Code changes often leave README files, changelogs, and docstrings outdated. This skill reviews completed implementation work and updates documentation where users need accurate guidance.
actual_capabilities: Reviews recent code changes with git diff context.
Classifies changes by README, CHANGELOG, docs, and docstring impact.
Updates README sections for public features, APIs, configuration, and breaking changes.
Creates changelog entries in conventional, Keep a Changelog, or simple formats.
Finds docs folder references to changed symbols and updates stale guidance.
Refreshes inline docstrings when function behavior, parameters, returns, or errors change.
limitations: It depends on clear repository history or an available diff.
It does not prove that every documentation example runs successfully.
It may need project-specific style guidance for unusual documentation formats.
It should not document private implementation details as public user features.

use_cases.title: Document a New Feature
use_cases.description: Update README, changelog, and usage examples after adding a public feature.

use_cases.title: Prepare Release Notes
use_cases.description: Turn completed implementation work into clear changelog entries before a release.

use_cases.title: Maintain API References
use_cases.description: Refresh docs and docstrings after public function signatures or behaviors change.

prompt_templates.title: Update Basic Docs
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request after a small feature change.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the latest implementation diff and update README and CHANGELOG only where the user-facing behavior changed.

prompt_templates.title: Refresh API Documentation
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request for changed public interfaces.
prompt_templates.prompt: Find public API changes in the last commit, update README usage examples, and adjust affected docs folder references.

prompt_templates.title: Align Docstrings
prompt_templates.prompt: Review modified functions and classes, then update docstrings for changed parameters, return values, exceptions, and examples.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Release Documentation
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request before a release or pull request.
prompt_templates.prompt: Classify all implementation changes, update release notes, README, docs, and docstrings, then summarize what changed and why.

output_examples.input: A new public authentication endpoint was added with examples in the implementation diff.
output: README receives a concise feature entry and updated usage guidance.
CHANGELOG receives a user-facing feature entry under the appropriate section.
Relevant docs pages and docstrings are checked for outdated authentication details.

output_examples.input: A function now requires a new configuration option and raises a new validation error.
output: API documentation describes the new option and default behavior.
Docstrings include the new parameter and validation error.
Examples are updated so users see the current call pattern.

output_examples.input: A refactor changed internal structure without user-facing behavior changes.
output_examples.output: The skill reports that public documentation does not need changes, while noting any docstrings that still need alignment.

best_practices: Review the implementation diff before editing documentation.
Document user-visible behavior instead of private implementation details.
Match the existing README, changelog, and docstring style.
anti_patterns: Adding changelog entries for formatting-only changes.
Updating examples without checking the new API shape.
Documenting internal refactors as public product changes.

faq.question: When should this skill run?
faq.answer: Run it after implementation work and before opening a pull request or release.

faq.question: Does it update every documentation file?
faq.answer: No. It updates files that relate to changed public behavior, APIs, examples, or docstrings.

faq.question: Can it write changelog entries?
faq.answer: Yes. It supports conventional changelogs, Keep a Changelog, and simple bullet formats.

faq.question: Does it create release notes automatically?
faq.answer: It can draft release-ready entries, but maintainers should review wording before publishing.

faq.question: Can it update inline docstrings?
faq.answer: Yes. It updates docstrings when parameters, returns, exceptions, or behavior changed.

faq.question: Does it run tests for examples?
faq.answer: It can recommend verification steps, but successful execution depends on the project setup.
